title: San Jose boss Arena expecting 'hell of a battle' against Houston
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutSan Jose boss Arena expecting 'hell of a battle' against HoustonShareAfter winning Game 1 of their round one MLS Cup playoff series, the San Jose Earthquakes travel to the Houston Dynamo on Saturday.San Jose Earthquakes head coach Bruce Arena anticipates "a hell of a battle" against the Houston Dynamo in Game 2 of their MLS Cup playoff series.
The Earthquakes won the opening encounter 2-1 at home after goals from Ronaldo Vieira and Eduard Lowen, with the latter netting with a stunning free-kick.
Victory marked San Jose's first playoff win since 2012, and they are now eyeing their first progression in the postseason since 2010.
Arena was delighted to see his side end their long wait for a playoff victory, but he knows they are now in for a stern test in Game 2.
"Everything's new here," Arena said. "We’re learning to be a good club.
"We’re learning to be a good team. Anything where we're moving in a good direction is positive.
"We're going to take the win and go to Houston and try to end the series in Houston. It's going to be a hell of a battle."
Any threat of a Houston comeback in Game 1 after Duncan McGuire's 80th-minute goal was cancelled out shortly after, with Agustin Resch shown a straight red card for a last-man foul.
Dynamo head coach Ben Olsen lamented his side's inability to stick to the plan last time out, something he hopes they have learned from ahead of Saturday's must-win fixture.
"The lessons learned are that if we stick to what we know, what we plan to do, then we are a pretty good team," said Olsen.
"But, if we deviate from that and we go on our own page, then we are not very good.
"It's a great format to lose a game, because you go home and you have to win a game, and the goal is to get back [to San Jose]."
McGuire came off the bench to score Houston's lone goal in Game 1 on Tuesday.
It was McGuire's 13th goal as a substitute in an MLS match (regular season and playoffs). No other MLS player has more than eight goals as a substitute since the beginning of the 2023 season.
On Tuesday, Lowen attempted five of San Jose's 11 shots, had three of their five shots on target and scored one of their two goals.
No other Earthquakes player has attempted three shots on target in a playoff match since Opta began detailed tracking of MLS in 2010.
Tuesday's 2–1 win stretched San Jose's unbeaten run against the Dynamo to five straight games (W3 D2). That is the Earthquakes' longest unbeaten streak across all competitions in the matchup.

Both of San Jose's goals were scored in the first 25 minutes of the match. It was the first time the Earthquakes scored multiple goals in the first 25 minutes of a playoff match and their fifth time doing so in an MLS match this season (did so four times in total between 2023 and 2025).
The defeat in Game 1 was Houston's third consecutive loss, equalling the Dynamo’s longest losing streak across all competitions this season (also March 21–April 11).
But Houston have not lost four straight matches since dropping four in a row in July and August 2022.
